prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly site that explains crypto in plain English, or (B) a site or educator that actually publishes its own trade/account P&L (including losses) so you can see real numbers? Those are different things — I can recommend the best for either.

Quick recommendations by purpose:

- If you want plain-English beginner education (clear articles/videos, walkthroughs):
  - Binance Academy — very beginner friendly, free, clear examples and diagrams.
  - CoinMarketCap Alexandria — short, plain explainers and glossaries.
  - Coin Bureau (YouTube + site) — long-form, plain-English primers and project deep dives.

- If you want on-chain data and real numeric metrics (including realized losses, supply flows, etc.):
  - Glassnode (Glassnode Studio & blog) — shows on‑chain metrics with charts and publishes realized-gain/loss metrics and writeups. More technical but gives real numbers.
  - CryptoQuant — similar on-chain datasets and loss/gain metrics.

- If you specifically want people/platforms that publish their actual trading performance (so you can see wins and losses in real numbers):
  - eToro (social/copy trading) — public trader stats and historical performance (including losing periods). Not a pure education site, but useful to observe real P&L.
  - Some independent traders/bloggers publish verified track records (look for those who provide exchange statements or open dashboards). If you want examples, say so and I’ll pull a few reputable names.

If you tell me which of the two you meant (education vs. public P&L), I’ll give a single best pick and link examples and what to watch out for.
